hook_text: A field became one of South Africa's biggest towns in just a few years. What was buried there?
clip_script: Kimberley, 1871. Diamonds are found on a small hill, and thousands of diggers rush in. The hill becomes the Big Hole, and a tent camp becomes a city. Gold built Johannesburg, coal built eMalahleni, fish built Lambert's Bay and trade built Durban. But laws also shaped where people lived. Under apartheid, families were forced out of places like District Six. Today, the law says people may live wherever they choose.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of South Africa with icons popping up: a diamond at Kimberley, gold at Johannesburg, a fish at Lambert's Bay, a ship at Durban, then a bulldozer at District Six.
mood: Lively at first, then serious about forced removals, ending with hope.
pacing: Quick rush of mining and fishing towns, then a slower, careful look at laws.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find one mining town, one fishing town and one port on a map of South Africa.
